items.title: Jerusalem's holy sites empty as Iran war upends Easter, Passover

featured_image.name: Jerusalem heads into a subdued Passover, Easter under the shadow war

items.description:
Jerusalem's Old City, normally teeming with pilgrims during the overlapping spring holidays, has fallen near-silent this year as the Iran-Israel war enters its sixth week, upending Easter and Passover observances in one of the world's holiest places.

Since the start of the U.S.-Israel military operation against Iran on February 28, Israeli authorities have barred access to the Old City for anyone other than residents and shop owners, according to the Times of Israel. Shops along the ancient stone streets sit shuttered under Home Front Command directives, and holy sites including the Western Wall, Al-Aqsa Mosque, and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre have been closed to the general public since March 6. Nationwide, gatherings remain limited to 100 people indoors and 50 outdoors, provided a bomb shelter can be reached within 90 seconds.[1][2][3]

items.title: Strikes on Iran's Mahshahr petrochemical zone kill 5, wound 170

featured_image.name: US and Israel strike petrochemical facilities in southwest Iran

items.description: US and Israeli airstrikes struck the Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Economic Zone in southwestern Iran on Saturday, killing at least five people and wounding 170 others in an attack targeting one of the country's most important industrial hubs. The Israel Defense Forces confirmed responsibility for the strikes, saying the complex housed "one of the primary locations where a critical component for ballistic missiles is produced."[1][2]

items.title: Nine-spin quantum system outperforms classical AI in weather forecasting

featured_image.name: Using Quantum Computing to Tell the Weather

items.description:
A quantum processor made from just nine atomic spins has beaten classical neural networks containing thousands of nodes at predicting real-world weather patterns, in what researchers describe as the first experimental demonstration of a quantum machine learning system outperforming large-scale classical models on a practical task.

The study, published in Physical Review Letters on Friday, was led by scientists at the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei, with collaborators at Fudan University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Zhejiang University.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran rejects Pakistan-led ceasefire talks with U.S., threatens second shipping chokepoint

featured_image.name: Iran's parliament speaker hints at targeting Bab el-Mandeb Strait

items.description: Diplomatic efforts to halt the widening conflict between the United States and Iran collapsed on Friday after Tehran formally rejected a Pakistan-brokered mediation initiative, refusing to send officials to Islamabad and dismissing Washington's demands as "unacceptable," according to The Wall Street Journal. The breakdown leaves no clear path to a ceasefire as violence in the region intensifies and global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains paralyzed.[1]

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills one in Gaza as ceasefire violations mount

featured_image.name: Israeli air strikes on Gaza kill four Palestinians - Al Jazeera

items.description:
Israeli forces struck a civilian vehicle at the entrance of the al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza on Saturday evening, killing one Palestinian man and injuring several others who were transported to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to the Palestinian news agency WAFA. The Middle East Monitor reported three others were wounded in the attack on Salah al-Din Street.[1][2]

The strike came on what Palestinian authorities count as the 177th day since the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas took effect in October 2025. Despite the deal, Israeli forces have continued near-daily airstrikes, drone attacks, artillery shelling, and naval fire across the Strip.

items.title: U.N. to vote on Hormuz resolution after France, Russia, China strip military language

featured_image.name: Bahrain waters down UN proposal over opposition to allowing force ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron warned Thursday that the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran cannot resolve Tehran's nuclear ambitions, calling instead for a diplomatic and regulatory framework that would include inspections and strict limits on uranium enrichment.

"A selective military action, even for a few weeks, will not resolve the nuclear issue in the long term," Macron said upon arriving in Seoul for a state visit to South Korea, according to AFP. "What is needed is the strictest possible framework to prevent further enrichment."[1][2]

Macron cautioned that without sustained diplomacy, the current crisis could repeat itself. "If there is no framework for diplomatic and technical negotiations, the situation can deteriorate again in a few months or a few years," he said.[3][1]
